name: Robert Nichols
bio: Robert Nichols (1893–1944) was an English poet who served as an artillery officer in the First World War and was invalided home. His war poems appeared in Invocation (1915) and Ardours and Endurances (1917).
He later taught English literature in Japan. His poem here comes from Untermeyer's Modern British Poetry (1920).

poems.title: Nearer
poems.author: Robert Nichols
poems.text:
Nearer and ever nearer ...
My body, tired but tense,
Hovers 'twixt vague pleasure
And tremulous confidence.

Arms to have and to use them
And a soul to be made
Worthy, if not worthy;
If afraid, unafraid.

To endure for a little,
To endure and have done:
Men I love about me,
Over me the sun!

And should at last suddenly
Fly the speeding death,
The four great quarters of heaven
Receive this little breath.
